items.summary_ko: 모바일 조작(MoMa) 로봇이 시연 수집 시 사용된 것과 정확히 동일한 기본 포즈에서 조작을 실행하기 어렵다는 문제점을 해결하기 위해, 동적 신규 뷰 합성(NVS)을 사용하여 시연을 증강하는 MOMASPLAT 방법이 제안되었습니다. 이는 정적 장면 가정을 극복합니다.
items.why_ko: 로봇의 모바일 조작 능력을 향상시키는 것은 다양한 실제 환경에서 로봇이 유연하게 작동하는 데 필수적이며, 이는 산업 및 서비스 로봇의 발전을 촉진합니다.

items.title: NPCBench: A Clinical Apprenticeship Benchmark for Multimodal Care-Pathway Reasoning in Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma
items.body: Current medical benchmarks typically break down clinical competence into isolated factual questions, single-image tasks, or static case vignettes. These tests score individual answers, but reveal less about whether a model can integrate subspecialty knowledge with multimodal evidence and track a patient's condition throughout a course of care. To close this gap, we introduce NPCBench, a clinical apprenticeship benchmark for nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC). NPCBench mirrors specialist training, from guideline and foundational knowledge to case planning, longitudinal review, CarePath integration, and open-ended consultation. It contains 4,777 component and consultation items and a 100-patient CarePath cohort with 417 scored diagnostic and care tasks. The episode-level evaluation tests whether diagnostic and care answers are jointly correct within a care pathway. By linking stepwise tasks to patient-level care trajectories, NPCBench evaluates whether models ground decisions in visual evidence, interpret changes in patient state, and meet clinical requirements in consultation. Across 30 evaluated models, we observe a composition gap: strong performance on individual tasks does not ensure jointly correct diagnostic and care answers for the same patient. Among 21 multimodal models, strict CarePath success reaches at most 23%. Paired controls and physician calibration further examine evidence grounding, longitudinal revision, and consultation judging. Overall, NPCBench broadens the evaluation of medical artificial intelligence beyond static question-answering paradigms to an apprenticeship-oriented assessment of clinical workflows, thereby offering a testbed for evidence-based and temporally coherent reasoning in oncology care.
items.title_ko: NPCBench: 비인두암 다중 모달 진료 경로 추론을 위한 임상 실습 벤치마크
items.summary_ko: 기존 의료 벤치마크의 한계를 극복하고, 모델이 다중 모달 증거와 전문 지식을 통합하여 환자의 상태를 추적할 수 있는지 평가하는 NPCBench가 비인두암 분야에서 소개되었습니다. 이는 실제 전문의 훈련을 반영합니다.
items.why_ko: 의료 AI 모델의 복합적인 임상 추론 능력을 평가하는 것은 오진율을 줄이고 환자 맞춤형 치료 계획 수립에 기여하며, 의료 AI의 신뢰성을 높이는 데 필수적입니다.

items.title: VisionSIM: Beyond Idealized Sensors - A Multi-Modal Simulator for Robot Perception
items.body: Robotic perception increasingly relies on heterogeneous sensor suites combining cameras with emerging modalities (event, SPAD, iToF/dToF, and thermal). Yet existing simulators idealize these sensors, hiding critical modality-specific failure modes that limit real-world deployment. We present VisionSIM, a unified, physically grounded simulation platform that elevates sensor realism to a first-class concern by modeling the raw physical measurement process for diverse conventional and emerging modalities. We expose fine-grained control over physical sensor parameters, reproducing failure modes overlooked by general-purpose simulators: pileup and glare for LiDAR; phase wrapping, saturation, and motion artifacts for iToF; refractory drops for event cameras; and history-dependent emission for thermal cameras. This enables principled cross-modality comparison on identical scenes and trajectories. We release the platform and a large indoor dataset with synchronized raw measurements and rich ground-truth annotations.
items.title_ko: VisionSIM: 이상적인 센서를 넘어선 로봇 인식을 위한 멀티모달 시뮬레이터
items.summary_ko: 기존 시뮬레이터가 센서를 이상적으로 모델링하여 실제 배포의 한계를 만드는 문제점을 해결하기 위해, 다양한 기존 및 신흥 모달리티 센서의 물리적 측정 과정을 모델링하는 VisionSIM이 제안되었습니다. 이는 센서 현실성을 높입니다.
items.why_ko: 로봇 인공지능 개발에서 실제 센서의 특성을 반영하는 시뮬레이터는 모델의 현실 적합성을 높여 실제 로봇 시스템 배포의 성공률을 향상시킵니다.

items.title: SHORE: Stability-Hybrid On-Policy Reinforcement Learning for Online Bin Packing
items.body: Online 3D bin packing with a processing buffer requires choosing which box to pack, its orientation, and its placement while keeping the stack stable under unknown future arrivals. A collapse ends the episode and forfeits the remaining volume. Existing methods use geometric rules or hard stability masks, limiting how risk can influence the joint choice of box, orientation, and placement. We propose Stability-Hybrid On-Policy Reinforcement Learning (SHORE), which combines a learned stability probability of a placement with an on-policy estimate of its return conditional on stability. A 3D U-Net learns stability from executed outcomes and simulated alternatives, revealing outcomes of actions underrepresented in early rollouts. A discrete on-policy actor--critic uses stability predictions in both its action values and policy prior, with gates that limit the effect of an untrained or changing model. In deployment, SHORE does not require additional search or simulation overhead. In Isaac Gym, SHORE reaches 73\% space utilization by 0.4M environment steps, while the same learner without stability modeling reaches that level at about 1M. On the expanded 60-box set, SHORE achieves 0.734 space utilization versus 0.588 for the GOPT state-of-the-art baseline, with a higher placement-failure frequency (1.03\% vs. 0.63\%), trading more risk for greater packed volume. The results show faster learning and higher utilization on the more demanding realistic box arrival set. Ablations suggest that simulated alternatives provide useful early supervision, while executed outcomes alone sustain later performance. We also demonstrate the method on a real robot to verify the simplicity of integrating the method to real bin packing pipelines.
items.title_ko: SHORE: 온라인 빈 패킹을 위한 안정성-하이브리드 온-폴리시 강화 학습
items.summary_ko: 미지의 미래 도착물에 대한 안정성을 유지하면서 상자를 패킹, 방향 지정 및 배치해야 하는 온라인 3D 빈 패킹 문제 해결을 위해, 학습된 안정성 확률과 정책을 결합한 SHORE(Stability-Hybrid On-Policy Reinforcement Learning)가 제안되었습니다.
items.why_ko: 강화 학습을 통해 3D 빈 패킹과 같은 복잡한 최적화 문제를 해결하는 것은 물류 및 제조 산업에서 효율성을 크게 높일 수 있습니다.

items.title: StrataFlux: Memory-Hierarchy-Native Low-Bit LLM Inference
items.body: Quantization reduces the memory and bandwidth demands of large language model (LLM) inference but can degrade accuracy; offloading higher-precision data can instead stall generation. We introduce StrataFlux, a framework that challenges this tradeoff by recovering accuracy lost to low-bit weight and key-value (KV) cache quantization while retaining quantization's memory and speed advantages. StrataFlux co-designs refinement representation, selection, and delivery to make host RAM and solid-state drives useful sources of additional precision. Its selective precision streaming reduces transfer volume, overlaps delivery with computation, and reuses fetched precision across decoding steps so generation need not wait for every transfer. We evaluate 2-4-bit weights and 2-3-bit KV-cache on dedicated GPUs and unified-memory platforms. For 2-bit Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct weights, StrataFlux reduces WikiText-2 perplexity from 9.46 to 8.40 while maintaining 95.4% of the quantized base's throughput on RTX 5090. With 2-bit weights and KV, StrataFlux raises Qwen3-8B's AIME 2024/2025 accuracy from 11.0% to 47.1% at unchanged GPU memory use. At 128K context, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct with 3-bit weights and 2-bit KV achieves comparable perplexity and speed to vLLM's 4-bit AWQ weights and 8-bit KV on RTX 5090, using approximately half the GPU memory. These results show that GPU-resident precision need not set the accuracy ceiling, nor offloading-tier latency dictate decoding speed.
items.title_ko: StrataFlux: 메모리 계층 구조에 최적화된 저비트 LLM 추론
items.summary_ko: 양자화로 인한 대규모 언어 모델(LLM) 추론 정확도 손실 문제를 해결하고, 양자화의 메모리 및 속도 이점을 유지하는 StrataFlux 프레임워크가 소개되었습니다. 이는 정제 표현, 선택 및 전달을 공동으로 설계합니다.
items.why_ko: LLM의 메모리 및 대역폭 요구 사항을 줄이면서도 정확도를 유지하는 것은 엣지 디바이스와 같은 자원 제약 환경에서 LLM을 배포하는 데 필수적인 기술입니다.

items.title: SpecCTMC: Exact Speculative Simulation of Diffusion Language Model Continuous-Time Markov Chains
items.body: Masked diffusion language models offer parallel text generation, but independently sampling multiple tokens can disrupt their dependencies and change the output distribution. Exact continuous-time sampling avoids this approximation, yet typically requires one sequential model evaluation per token. We introduce SpecCTMC, a training-free speculative sampler that reduces this sequential bottleneck without a separate draft model. SpecCTMC proposes successive token updates using previously computed model predictions, evaluates their intermediate states in parallel, and applies an exact acceptance-and-correction procedure. We prove that SpecCTMC preserves the joint distribution of event times, generation order, and token values of the underlying continuous-time Markov chain. It therefore introduces neither time-discretization error nor additional factorization error from parallel decoding. Experiments on LLaDA-8B-Instruct and Dream-v0-Instruct-7B across five benchmarks demonstrate 1.73-4.38x fewer sequential model evaluations than direct continuous-time sampling, while preserving the reference sampling distribution. Our code is available at: https://github.com/kasakh/specctmc
items.title_ko: SpecCTMC: 확산 언어 모델 연속 시간 마르코프 체인의 정확한 투기적 시뮬레이션
items.summary_ko: 확산 언어 모델의 병렬 텍스트 생성에서 토큰 간 종속성 문제를 해결하기 위해, 별도의 드래프트 모델 없이 순차적 병목 현상을 줄이는 SpecCTMC라는 훈련 없는 투기적 샘플러가 소개되었습니다. 이는 이전에 계산된 측정된 결합을 사용하여 연속적인 토큰 업데이트를 제안합니다.
items.why_ko: 확산 모델의 생성 속도를 높이고 병렬성을 활용하는 것은 대규모 텍스트 생성의 효율성을 향상시키는 데 기여합니다.

items.title: Unifying Central Flow, Rod Flow, and the Edge Coupling
items.body: At the edge of stability, the iterates of gradient descent oscillate along the sharp directions of the Hessian. This poses a significant challenge for continuous-time models as the usual continuous-time approximation -- the gradient flow -- admits no oscillations. Several continuous-time models have been proposed to capture the behavior at the edge of stability, among them central flow and rod flow. Although both models can be interpreted as performing a coarse-graining in time, the connection between them remains poorly understood. Here we show that both flows can be derived from a third object, the edge coupling: a functional on consecutive iterates whose critical points are the fixed points and period-two orbits of gradient descent. It is revealed that the two flows correspond to coarse-grainings at different time scales. Rod flow coarse-grains over only the fastest time scale, while central flow coarse-grains over both the fast and intermediate time scales. Furthermore, using the edge coupling, we derive rod flows and central flows for momentum methods such as heavy ball and Adam. We verify the derived flows experimentally on representative neural network architectures, where they track the discrete iterates throughout all phases of training -- including the transition from the stable regime to the edge of stability.
items.title_ko: 중앙 흐름, 로드 흐름, 엣지 결합의 통합
items.summary_ko: 경사 하강법의 반복이 헤시안의 날카로운 방향을 따라 진동하는 안정성 경계면에서의 동작을 포착하기 위해 제안된 중앙 흐름과 로드 흐름 모델을 통합하는 연구입니다. 이들은 시간 스케일에서 거친 입자화를 수행하는 것으로 해석될 수 있습니다.
items.why_ko: 최적화 알고리즘의 이론적 이해를 깊게 하는 연구로, 이는 AI 모델 학습의 안정성과 효율성을 개선하는 데 필요한 기초 지식입니다.

items.title: USB Gym: A Gymnasium Testbed for Closed-Loop Ultrasound View Matching
items.body:
Background and Objective: Our main goal is ultrasound guidance: moving a probe until its image matches a target view. Published methods for each part of a guide are evaluated in separate simulators. We asked whether these methods, combined into one guide, are good enough.
Methods: We built USB Gym, a testbed whose standard engine simulates ultrasound from public patient CT, with a network drawing organ textures from CT labels. Its guide has three replaceable parts (slots), an organ segmenter, a controller and a reward, which received 20 published methods, each run on the same 60 episodes of six held-out patients. In each slot, a published method replaced ours only if detectably better on these patients. The better of this combination and our original guide on 20 new CTs is the benchmark baseline. A pose oracle, reading the exact probe pose available only in simulation, set the reference. The results below are exploratory.
Results: On these CTs, the probe started on average 16.0 mm from the target view; the pose oracle brought it to 1.5 mm. Of the results known when the combination was fixed, only an image-similarity reward (SSIM) was slightly but detectably better, so the combination was our guide with that reward. This combination was the benchmark baseline, ending at 13.7 mm (16% of the oracle's progress).
Conclusions: Combining untuned published methods with ours did not guide the probe near the target view; the task remains under-explored. The testbed accepts new methods; no guide was tested on hardware.
items.title_ko: USB Gym: 폐루프 초음파 뷰 매칭을 위한 체육관 테스트베드
items.summary_ko: 초음파 가이던스(프로브를 이동하여 목표 뷰와 일치시키는)의 각 부분에 대한 기존 방법들을 결합하여 평가하는 테스트베드 USB Gym이 구축되었습니다. 이 테스트베드는 표준 엔진으로 CT 스캔에서 초음파를 시뮬레이션합니다.
items.why_ko: 의료 로봇 및 가이던스 시스템 개발에서 다양한 구성 요소를 통합하여 실제 환경에 가깝게 평가할 수 있는 시뮬레이션 환경은 연구 개발 속도를 가속화할 수 있습니다.

items.title: 4D Point Splatting for mmWave Radar Micro-Doppler Differentiable Rendering
items.body: Millimeter-wave radar resolves the micrometer displacements of a moving body as micro-Doppler, enabling gait, gesture, activity, pose and vital-sign sensing. Each task relies on a downstream model trained on real data, yet radar datasets lag orders of magnitude behind vision and language. Brute-force collection will not close that gap, and existing synthesis methods (forward-only simulators, learned generators and static-scene inverse renderers) cannot fit a real capture of a moving body, leaving a sim2real gap. We present 4D Point Splatting (4DPS), a physics-based differentiable renderer that fits an explicit moving scene to a real capture. Using the synchronized camera to initialize the room and body, we represent the scene as oriented points carrying material, normal and velocity, and splat each point into range and Doppler bins. Our output is the raw complex return a real radar records, so we apply the same signal processing on the rendered data to obtain any representation for training any SOTA downstream model. We fit 235 sequences on HuPR and 100 on RT-Pose, two datasets with different radars. Our reconstructions set the state of the art, with median correlations of 0.940 and 0.830 on range-azimuth, 0.829 and 0.695 on range-Doppler, and 0.988 and 0.966 on micro-Doppler. Our renders also set the state of the art in downstream sim2real gap. On RT-Pose, a pose model trained on them reaches 21.9 cm MPJPE on real data, against 16.7 cm for real training and 127.6 cm for the RF-Genesis baseline, where both the rendered- and real-trained models learn nearly the same features. Our custom CUDA kernels fit a sequence in 5.7 minutes on HuPR and 12.9 on RT-Pose on one H100, making dataset-scale inverse rendering of mmWave radar possible for the first time. This work can enable synthetic data generation for any human-centered downstream task and model, and scene editing for data augmentation.
items.title_ko: 4D 포인트 스플래팅: mmWave 레이더 마이크로 도플러 미분 렌더링
items.summary_ko: 밀리미터파 레이더의 마이크로 도플러를 활용하여 움직이는 물체의 미세 변위를 해결하는 4D 포인트 스플래팅 방법이 제안되었습니다. 이는 보행, 제스처, 활동 감지 등에 사용되는 레이더 데이터셋 부족 문제를 해결하기 위한 것입니다.
items.why_ko: 레이더 데이터를 효율적으로 합성하고 렌더링하는 기술은 자율 주행, 보안, 헬스케어 등 레이더 기반 AI 애플리케이션 개발에 필수적입니다.

items.title: Enhancing Local and Global Structure in Compressed AI Agent Memory
items.body: AI agents store text as embedding vectors and compress them at scale. A compression is accepted when each item's nearest neighbors survive, but agents also consolidate, delete, and compare memories, tasks that depend on which items lie far apart. We evaluate both ends with two label-free fidelities from our prior work: the local fidelity $L$ at 10 neighbors and the global fidelity $G$ at 30 to 50 percent of the memory. At 96 bytes per passage, rescored binary codes reach an $L$ of 0.97 yet move 10.1 percent of passages to another theme; PCA with 8-bit codes, at an $L$ of 0.77, moves 1.7 percent. Rescoring leaves the stored codes, and thus $G$, unchanged. We prove that across the $G$ band, $1-ν_k$ is at most 2 to 2.18 times the square root of the near-far rank-violation rate, and that this rate follows the distance noise of the compression (correlation 0.979). Our locality-aware quantization (LAQ) turns the bound into a hinge objective on the codebooks of an OPQ index, keeping its bytes, rotation, and search. To our knowledge, LAQ is the first quantizer whose objective comes from a proven bound on the far end. Reconstruction alone raises $G$ in 0 of 52 held-out runs; the far hinge raises it in all 52. LAQ raises $G$ in all 52 ($p=8.5\times 10^{-4}$ over 13 memory-encoder groups), including the external FinDER memory, has the highest $G$ of seven equal-size quantizers in all 12 Multi-Doc-2025 runs, scales to a million passages, and keeps evidence recall.
items.title_ko: 압축된 AI 에이전트 메모리의 로컬 및 글로벌 구조 강화
items.summary_ko: AI 에이전트 메모리 압축 시 근접 이웃 보존뿐 아니라, 메모리 항목 간의 거리 관계를 유지하여 로컬 및 글로벌 충실도를 높이는 방법을 연구합니다. 이는 메모리 압축의 품질을 다각도로 평가합니다.
items.why_ko: 에이전트의 장기 기억 및 추론 능력을 향상시키기 위한 메모리 관리 기술은 복잡한 AI 에이전트 시스템 개발에 있어 매우 중요합니다.

items.title: Discovering Learning Rules that Shape Others
items.body: In general-sum games, self-interested learners can reach outcomes that are poor for everyone, which has motivated methods that shape the opponent's learning. Methods like Learning with Opponent-Learning Awareness (LOLA), which differentiates through the opponent's learning process, and Model-Free Opponent Shaping (M-FOS), which uses model-free optimisation methods for long-horizon opponent shaping, have enabled mutual cooperation and exploitation of learners. However, these methods require access to the opponent's parameters, policy, rewards or learning rule during deployment. In single-agent reinforcement learning, update rules discovered by meta-learning have achieved state-of-the-art results (e.g. DiscoRL). These rules are separate from the policy they train and read only the agent's own experience. We hereby extend this framework to general-sum settings by introducing Discovered Update Rule for Opponent Shaping (DUOS). To the best of our knowledge, this is the first method to discover an update rule for an agent in general-sum games. DUOS meta-trains the rule to maximise the agent's expected return over its lifetime, and updates an inner network using the agent's own experience. We show that our discovered rule exhibits behaviour consistent with opponent shaping without reading opponent policies or parameters, and ranks 1st in normalised mean score and 1st in self-play among tournament entrants.
items.title_ko: 타인의 학습 규칙을 형성하는 학습 규칙 발견
items.summary_ko: 일반 합 게임에서 이기적인 학습자가 모두에게 좋지 않은 결과를 초래할 수 있다는 문제의식에서 출발하여, 상대방의 학습 과정을 통해 차별화하는 LOLA(Learning with Opponent-Learning Awareness)와 같은 방법들이 제안되었습니다. 이 연구는 상대방의 학습 규칙을 형성하는 방법을 탐구합니다.
items.why_ko: 다중 에이전트 시스템에서 협력과 경쟁을 최적화하기 위한 학습 규칙을 설계하는 것은 게임 AI, 경제 모델링, 자율 시스템 등 다양한 분야에 응용될 수 있습니다.

items.title: Cultural Adaptation within Repeated Social Interactions
items.body: Much of human culture is tacit and is typically learned through situated social interaction. As LLMs are deployed as interactive agents across diverse communities, assessing their cultural competence demands moving beyond existing question-answering approaches, shifting from what they know to how they adapt. In this work, we broaden the scope of cultural adaptation in NLP by investigating whether LLMs can adapt through repeated interactions via a sandbox environment. By reframing cultural adaptation as a continuous process of norm assimilation through social interaction, our work demonstrates that memory mechanisms foster longitudinal learning across repeated interactions, facilitate transfer to different social settings, and enable multilingual norm assimilation across five languages. Together, our findings lay the groundwork for continuous, interaction-driven cultural adaptation in LLMs.
items.title_ko: 반복적인 사회적 상호작용 속에서의 문화 적응
items.summary_ko: LLM이 다양한 커뮤니티에서 상호작용하는 에이전트로 배포됨에 따라, 그들의 문화적 역량을 평가하기 위해 기존의 질문-답변 방식을 넘어 반복적인 상호작용을 통해 문화에 적응하는 능력을 연구합니다. 샌드박스 환경을 활용합니다.
items.why_ko: AI 에이전트가 다양한 문화적 맥락에서 인간과 효과적으로 상호작용하고 적응하는 능력은 글로벌 AI 서비스 개발에 필수적이며, AI의 사회적 지능을 높이는 데 기여합니다.

items.title: Polarity Classification with Multitask Learning Syntax Augmentation
items.body: Sentiment Analysis (SA) is a fundamental NLP task concerned with the identification and categorization of subjective information in text. While lexicon-based methods offer transparency, they often struggle with linguistic phenomena such as negation and intensification. Syntactic parsing has been integrated into SA pipelines to address this, but conventional parsers introduce significant computational overhead. Recent work shows that reformulating dependency parsing as a Sequence Labeling (SEL) task can improve efficiency. We propose and compare two strategies for integrating syntactic knowledge into a neural sentiment analysis model under unified Multi-Task Learning (MTL). The first, Standard-MTL, jointly learns dependency parsing (via sequence labeling) and sentiment polarity classification using a shared encoder with two task-specific heads. The second, Contrastive-MTL, provides implicit syntactic guidance through a contrastive auxiliary objective and a syntax-biased attention pooling mechanism, without requiring explicit label prediction. Both rely on syntactic annotations during training and eliminate need for hand-crafted compositional rules or external parsing at inference. We evaluate eleven datasets spanning seven languages---the MARC corpus (English, Spanish, French, German) and seven datasets from SemEval-2022 Task 10 (English, Spanish, Norwegian, Basque, Catalan)---using four established SEL encodings. With the relative encoding, Contrastive-MTL outperforms a syntax-naive baseline on 10 of 11 datasets and surpasses the external rule-based pipeline (SELSP) that parses at inference on all six datasets where the latter applies, while being 1.5--9$\times$ faster at evaluation. Standard-MTL is more dataset- and encoding-dependent. These results show implicit syntactic supervision during training can match or exceed explicit parsing at inference without computational overhead.
items.title_ko: 다중 작업 학습 구문 증강을 통한 극성 분류
items.summary_ko: 감성 분석(SA)에서 어휘 기반 방법의 한계를 해결하기 위해, 구문 분석을 다중 작업 학습(Multitask Learning)과 통합하는 방법이 제안되었습니다. 이는 구문 분석을 시퀀스 레이블링으로 재구성하여 계산 오버헤드를 줄입니다.
items.why_ko: 감성 분석 모델의 정확도를 높이는 것은 챗봇, 고객 리뷰 분석 등 다양한 NLP 애플리케이션에 중요하며, 계산 효율성 개선은 실제 배포에 유리합니다.

items.title: Learning the Task or Learning the Verifier? Rethinking Criteria Exposure in Embodied Self-Improvement
items.body: Self-improving embodied agents are increasingly being developed and compared on robot simulation benchmarks. Several recent works expose the benchmark's success criteria to the learning agent, a practice we call Criteria Exposure (CE). These criteria, originally written to verify policies trained by imitation learning, often demand more than the corresponding language instructions, so a score from such a verifier may not faithfully reflect whether the instructed task was completed, especially for robot-control programs written by an agent. As embodied coding agents report ever higher benchmark scores, a natural question arises: when a coding agent is exposed to the benchmark's criteria, does it generate code that better performs the instructed task, or code that simply overfits to the verification criteria? We conduct controlled experiments with a self-improving agent with and without CE, and find that with CE the agent quickly produces code with a higher success rate under the given criteria, but this advantage disappears when the criteria are changed slightly without departing from the original instructions. More importantly, the skills the agent develops under CE transfer poorly across tasks. We further propose instruction-faithful criteria and show that they better reflect the performance of agent-generated programs.
items.title_ko: 과제를 학습하는가, 검증자를 학습하는가? 체화된 자기 개선에서 기준 노출 재고
items.summary_ko: 자기 개선 체화 에이전트가 로봇 시뮬레이션 벤치마크에서 평가될 때, 벤치마크의 성공 기준을 에이전트에게 노출하는 '기준 노출(Criteria Exposure)' 관행이 과제 학습과 검증자 학습 사이의 혼란을 야기할 수 있음을 지적합니다. 이는 정책 검증과 실제 과제 완료 간의 불일치를 초래합니다.
items.why_ko: AI 에이전트의 벤치마크 평가 방식에 대한 비판적 고찰은 모델의 실제 성능을 정확히 측정하고 과적합을 방지하는 데 필수적입니다.

items.title: Benchmarking Large Language Models on Heterogeneous Cognitive and Biomedical Knowledge Graphs: The Role of Graph Grounding in Multi-Hop Reasoning and Hallucination Mitigation
items.body: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used in biomedical and cognitive neuroscience, but their ability to reason reliably over heterogeneous knowledge graphs (KGs) remains unclear. We benchmark five LLMs (GPT-5.1, Gemini 2.0 Pro, Llama 3, Qwen, and BioGPT) across five KGs: DrugBank, NeuroSynth, Cognitive Atlas, Brain Map, and GDPKG. We introduce a multitier query dataset to evaluate reasoning depth and factual accuracy under KG-aware (graph-grounded) and KG-agnostic conditions. Inter-annotator agreement was substantial, with Cohen's kappa of 0.781 (range: 0.753-0.807) and Fleiss' kappa of 0.77. Results show that general-purpose models, particularly GPT-5.1 and Gemini 2.0 Pro, generally outperform domain-specific models on multi-hop and high-level reasoning tasks, although performance declines as query complexity increases. KG grounding reduces hallucination rates across all evaluated models. Contrary to our initial hypothesis, domain-specific models do not consistently outperform general-purpose models on specialized tasks without graph grounding. These findings highlight the value of combining broad language-model capabilities with structured domain knowledge. We provide practical guidance for selecting LLM-KG integration strategies based on task complexity and computational constraints, and discuss hybrid neurosymbolic architectures for personalized medicine, cognitive disorder diagnosis, and explainable AI.
items.title_ko: 이기종 인지 및 생의학 지식 그래프에서 LLM 벤치마킹: 다중 홉 추론 및 환각 완화에서 그래프 접지 역할
items.summary_ko: LLM이 이기종 지식 그래프(KG)에서 얼마나 신뢰할 수 있게 추론할 수 있는지 평가하기 위해, DrugBank, NeuroSynth 등 5개 KG에서 5개 LLM(GPT-5.1, Gemini 2.0 Pro, Llama 3 등)을 벤치마킹합니다. KG 인식 및 KG 비인식 조건에서 추론 깊이와 사실 정확도를 평가합니다.
items.why_ko: LLM이 복잡한 지식 그래프를 활용하여 정확하고 일관된 정보를 생성하는 능력은 의료, 과학 연구 등 고정밀이 요구되는 분야에서 AI의 활용도를 높이는 데 결정적입니다.

items.title: Interpretable many-body interaction laws for collective motion from few trajectories
items.body: Models of collective motion usually reduce social interactions to pairwise forces, despite empirical evidence for many-body effects. We introduce the directional atomic cluster expansion (dACE), which adapts the atomic cluster expansion (ACE) of interatomic potentials to self-propelled agents. dACE provides a systematically improvable, exactly equivariant expansion of an agent's acceleration that splits uniquely into 1-, 2-, 3-body and higher contributions, along with a self term for the agent's own past motion that is fitted so that it does not absorb the interactions. On simulated collectives in two and three dimensions with known rules, dACE recovers the interaction law body order by body order from little data, while the neural model SocialNet, the current closest competitor, needs more data, has much larger errors on many-body or chiral rules and is restricted to 2D. On real data sets of tracked zebrafish and golden shiners, the laws learned by dACE agree better between disjoint halves of the data than SocialNet's. The learned laws are interpretable, and in the shiners the 3-body term opposes the pairwise response as neighbourhoods get dense. Finally, we show that next-step prediction accuracy mostly measures self-propulsion and noise rather than the interactions, and suggest more robust combinations of error measures for interaction learning.
items.title_ko: 소수의 궤적에서 집단 운동을 위한 해석 가능한 다체 상호작용 법칙 발견
items.summary_ko: 집단 운동 모델에서 쌍별 힘이 아닌 다체 효과를 고려하기 위해, 원자 클러스터 확장(ACE)을 자율 이동 에이전트에 적용한 dACE(directional atomic cluster expansion)가 소개되었습니다. 이는 1, 2, 3체 및 그 이상의 기여로 분리될 수 있는 가속도 확장을 제공합니다.
items.why_ko: 집단 지능, 로봇 군집 등 여러 에이전트가 상호작용하는 시스템을 모델링하고 이해하는 데 중요한 기여를 하며, AI의 복잡한 시스템 제어 능력을 향상시킵니다.

items.title: LLM-Assisted Label Noise Correction for EEG-Based Sleep Stage Classification
items.body: Automatic sleep stage classification from electroencephalography (EEG) signals is a critical task in clinical sleep medicine. While deep learning models have shown promising results in this domain, their performance is fundamentally constrained by the quality of training labels, which human experts manually annotate and that are subject to inter-rater disagreement and systematic labeling errors. In this paper, we propose a novel LLM-assisted label-noise filtering pipeline that operates exclusively during training to identify and remove unreliable sleep-stage annotations before retraining the classifier. Specifically, TinySleepNet is first trained on the original dataset to extract per-epoch SoftMax confidence scores, then low-confidence epochs are submitted to LLaMA 3.1 along with their EEG spectral features and surrounding sequence context. The LLM evaluates each epoch against AASM sleep-scoring guidelines and assigns a verdict of RELIABLE or SUSPICIOUS. Suspicious epochs are removed from the training set, and TinySleepNet is retrained on the cleaned data. Evaluated on the Sleep-EDF Expanded dataset using 20-fold cross-validation, our method improves overall accuracy from 81.8% to 84.6% and Macro F1-score from 75.6% to 77.4%, with particularly notable gains in REM detection. Crucially, because the LLM operates only during training, the lightweight TinySleepNet architecture (1.3M parameters) is preserved at inference, making the proposed pipeline suitable for real-time, wearable sleep monitoring applications.
items.title_ko: LLM 지원 레이블 노이즈 보정을 통한 EEG 기반 수면 단계 분류
items.summary_ko: EEG 신호 기반 수면 단계 자동 분류에서 전문가 수동 주석의 노이즈 문제를 해결하기 위해, LLM 지원 레이블 노이즈 필터링 파이프라인이 제안되었습니다. 이는 오로지 노이즈가 있는 주석만으로 작동합니다.
items.why_ko: 의료 데이터의 노이즈는 AI 모델의 성능을 저해하는 주요 원인이므로, LLM을 활용하여 레이블 노이즈를 보정하는 기술은 의료 AI의 신뢰성과 정확도를 높이는 데 기여합니다.

items.title: RM-VLM: From Natural-Language Task Descriptions to Vision-Grounded Reward Machines
items.body: Reward machines (RMs) have been proposed as a reward formulation in reinforcement learning (RL) to capture non-Markovian tasks where credit assignment depends on history. By representing reward functions as automata, RMs expose the task's temporal structure and allow such rewards to be handled within a Markovian framework. However, they assume a labelling function, a proposition-grounding oracle for observations, which must be manually engineered for each environment, limiting their wider applicability. In this work, we address this limitation by proposing RM-VLM, a novel approach in which a large language model (LLM) generates an RM from a natural-language task description, and a vision-language model (VLM) acts as the labelling function, grounding the RM's propositions over image-based observations during RM-guided policy learning. A VLM-based value function estimator is used to assess the agent's progress towards each RM transition and derive a dense reward signal. We evaluate RM-VLM on three domains covering non-Markovian grid-world navigation, robotic manipulation, and 3D object collection. Our experimental results show that RM-VLM consistently achieves higher task success rates than existing VLM-based reward methods across all tested domains.
items.title_ko: RM-VLM: 자연어 작업 설명에서 비전 기반 보상 머신으로
items.summary_ko: 강화 학습에서 비 마르코프적인 작업을 포착하는 보상 머신(RM)의 활용을 위해, 수동으로 엔지니어링해야 했던 라벨링 함수를 자연어 작업 설명에서 자동으로 생성하는 RM-VLM 방법이 제안되었습니다. 이는 보상 함수를 오토마타로 표현합니다.
items.why_ko: 자연어 명령으로 복잡한 비 마르코프적 작업을 로봇이나 에이전트에게 가르치는 것은 인간-AI 상호작용의 자연스러움을 높이고 강화 학습의 적용 범위를 확장하는 데 중요합니다.

items.title: Measured Coupling for Parallel Decoding in Diffusion Language Models
items.body: Diffusion language models can write many tokens per step, but must choose which tokens are safe to commit together. Mean-field decoding penalizes pairs of positions whose predictions look alike. We replace this proxy with the coupling itself: how much committing one token changes the model's confidence at another. Cheap probes inside the main forward pass measure it, with no training or extra model, and it plugs into the same mean-field rule. On three models and four benchmarks, our method needs far fewer steps than mean-field decoding and is faster in most settings, also with a key-value cache, at an average accuracy cost of 1.1 points. Shuffling the couplings or replacing them with a uniform bonus loses this gain.
items.title_ko: 확산 언어 모델의 병렬 디코딩을 위한 측정된 결합
items.summary_ko: 확산 언어 모델이 단계별로 여러 토큰을 작성할 때, 어떤 토큰들을 함께 커밋해도 안전한지 선택하는 문제를 해결하기 위해 '결합' 자체를 측정하는 방법이 제안되었습니다. 이는 추가 모델 없이 메인 포워드 패스 내부에서 계산됩니다.
items.why_ko: 병렬 디코딩의 효율성을 높이고 생성 품질을 유지하는 것은 확산 모델의 실제 응용을 가속화하며, 대규모 텍스트 생성의 속도를 개선합니다.

items.title: First-Token Attraction in Mamba Dynamics
items.body: We study token dynamics in deep Mamba models, with a particular focus on the attracting role of the first token. Unlike attention mechanisms, where token interactions are governed by positive scalar coefficients, Mamba dynamics involve full matrix-valued interaction coefficients with no positivity or definiteness guarantees. This structural difference makes Mamba dynamics substantially harder to analyze and prevents the direct application of existing techniques for attention-based models. To overcome this challenge, we introduce a new analytical framework based on a high-dimensional invariant box and a sharp exit-time argument, which together recover an effective form of sign-definiteness. Using this framework, we characterize the possible limit points of token trajectories and prove explicit exponential convergence rates. Our analysis reveals that the first token has privileged dynamics: its limiting direction attracts subsequent tokens, inducing token clustering and attention-sink phenomena in deep Mamba models. We further show that this attraction mechanism extends to broader sequence dynamics, including state-space models, causal attention, and classical time-series models. Experiments on Falcon-Mamba-7B validate our predictions, showing that concentration on the first token increases with depth and dominates in later layers.
items.title_ko: Mamba 동역학에서 첫 토큰의 인력
items.summary_ko: 깊은 Mamba 모델에서 토큰 동역학, 특히 첫 토큰의 인력 역할을 연구합니다. Mamba의 행렬 값 상호작용 계수는 기존 어텐션 메커니즘과 달라 분석이 더 복잡합니다.
items.why_ko: Mamba와 같은 새로운 아키텍처의 내부 작동 방식을 이해하는 것은 모델을 더 잘 설계하고 최적화하는 데 중요하며, 이는 더 효율적인 AI 모델 개발로 이어집니다.

items.title: Dynamic Optimistic Constrained OCO with Memory via Delay Equivalence
items.body: Online Convex Optimization with memory and time-varying constraints (COCO-M) is a recently-introduced framework that captures the dynamics of stateful online learning and non-stochastic control with budget constraints. Despite its expressive power, COCO-M remains largely understudied. In this work, we tackle this problem in its full scale, providing an optimistic algorithm that incorporates untrusted predictions to tame universal dynamic regret and cumulative constraint violation. Our analysis leverages a potent reduction from memory to delay and treats state-dependent gradients as delayed feedback. We establish the first bounds that adapt to both environment non-stationarity (path length $P_T$) and prediction accuracy, while lifting previous restrictive assumptions such as functional separability. En route to these results, we derive findings of independent interest for the memory-to-delay reduction, and for delayed OCO with time-varying constraints. The proposed framework ensures sublinear worst-case guarantees that improve with prediction accuracy, reaching $\mathcal O(1)$ regret under perfect predictions, with cumulative constraint violation (CCV) $\mathcal O(\sqrt{T})$ for unknown $P_T$ and $\mathcal O(\log T)$ for known or online observable $P_T$ , while recovering the optimal COCO rates when memory disappears.
items.title_ko: 지연 등가성을 통한 메모리를 갖춘 동적 낙관적 제약 OCO
items.summary_ko: 메모리와 시간 가변 제약 조건을 가진 온라인 볼록 최적화(COCO-M) 프레임워크를 다루며, 신뢰할 수 없는 예측을 통합하여 동적 후회(dynamic regret) 및 누적 제약 조건 위반을 제어하는 낙관적 알고리즘을 제안합니다.
items.why_ko: 온라인 학습 및 제어 시스템에서 메모리와 제약 조건을 다루는 것은 자율 에이전트의 안정적이고 효율적인 의사 결정에 필수적입니다.

items.title: Transformer-Based Trajectory Prescription for sEMG-Optimizing Robot-Mediated Rehabilitation
items.body: Robot-mediated rehabilitation has the potential to deliver high-intensity, individualized therapy, but existing systems (which have not consistently improved outcomes) typically prescribe kinematic trajectories rather than explicitly targeting the neuromotor activations thought to support recovery. To address this gap, and ultimately enable activation-optimizing rehabilitation robot behavior, we present a personalizable transformer-based model mapping individuals' muscle activations (as measured via surface electromyography) to prescribed contact force trajectories when interacting with an end-effector rehabilitation robot. The model uses a transformer encoder-decoder leveraging rotary positional embeddings (RoPE) to generate a latent representation of trajectory-relevant and user-specific neuromotor factors, and augments trajectory prediction with flow matching to produce a distribution over plausible prescriptions biased toward the training distribution. Using data from 16 healthy participants completing 15 isometric trajectory tracking tasks, we evaluate generalization across held-out tasks and users, as well as the feasibility of user-specific fine-tuning within a therapy-session timescale. The model achieves mean trajectory prediction errors of <8% on held out tasks and users, with effectively instantaneous deterministic inference and sub-second sampling of trajectory distributions. An initial test using the model during live rehabilitation tasks demonstrates that, on average, participants reach the target neuromotor activations with just 15% error accumulated throughout the task. These results provide a proof of concept for data-driven, activation-targeted trajectory prescription in robot-mediated rehabilitation and establish a foundation for future validation in clinical populations. Data and code have been open-sourced as part of the OpenRobotRehab project on SimTK.
items.title_ko: sEMG 최적화 로봇 매개 재활을 위한 트랜스포머 기반 궤적 처방
items.summary_ko: 로봇 매개 재활에서 신경 운동 활성화를 명시적으로 목표로 삼기 위해, 개인의 근육 활성도(sEMG)를 로봇 궤적으로 매핑하는 개인화 가능한 트랜스포머 기반 모델이 제시되었습니다. 이는 재활 치료 효과를 높이는 데 기여할 수 있습니다.
items.why_ko: AI 기반 로봇이 환자 맞춤형 재활 치료를 제공함으로써 치료 효과를 극대화하고 의료 서비스를 혁신할 잠재력을 보여줍니다.

items.title: AutoCompress: Automated Hardware-Guided Model Compression
items.body: LLM pruning must preserve quality while meeting hardware- and workload-specific constraints on latency, throughput, and memory. Existing pruning workflows often target parameter counts, requiring practitioners to manually select model sizes that meet latency, throughput, and GPU memory limits. However, parameter count alone does not predict these metrics, which depend on the model architecture, workload, hardware, and serving engine. We introduce AutoCompress, a hardware-guided compression framework that directly incorporates such constraints into differentiable architecture search. AutoCompress jointly optimizes global and per-layer structure to produce heterogeneous architectures, guided by serving-engine cost models validated against end-to-end latency, throughput, and memory measurements. We evaluate AutoCompress on long-context local coding, batched datacenter serving, and latency-sensitive in-game interaction. Compared to the state-of-the-art Minitron pruning framework, AutoCompress improves average accuracy across eight benchmarks by 6.57, 2.35, and 0.57 percentage points on RTX 5070, RTX 5080, and H100, respectively. AutoCompress also compresses Nemotron 3.5 Super from 120B to 74B parameters for single-B200 BF16 serving at 128K context, retaining 95% of its mean benchmark score.
items.title_ko: AutoCompress: 하드웨어 유도 모델 압축 자동화
items.summary_ko: LLM 가지치기가 품질을 유지하면서 하드웨어 및 워크로드 특정 제약 조건(지연 시간, 처리량, 메모리)을 충족해야 하는 문제에 직면합니다. AutoCompress는 이러한 하드웨어 유도 압축을 자동화하는 프레임워크를 제시합니다.
items.why_ko: AI 모델의 실용적인 배포를 위해 하드웨어 제약을 고려한 모델 최적화는 필수적이며, AutoCompress는 이러한 복잡한 과정을 자동화하여 개발자의 생산성을 높입니다.

items.title: A Generative Model of Contextual Integrity: Appropriate vs. Inappropriate Information Sharing
items.body: Contextual integrity (CI) holds that appropriate information flow depends on context-specific norms. The same disclosure may be appropriate in one context and inappropriate in another. We build a generative model of contextual integrity to study information sharing through simulated conversations. Two actors played by large language models exchange messages, with one holding private information and the other seeking it. We examine how sharing and refusal vary with the situation, the holder's decision logic, disposition, and the underlying language model. Actors shared information with the rightful recipients when it was needed, but also disclosed it to people who were not entitled to receive it. The model provides a way to study how disclosure and refusal develop through conversation as the situations and the actors vary.
items.title_ko: 맥락적 무결성(Contextual Integrity)의 생성 모델: 적절한 정보 공유 vs. 부적절한 정보 공유
items.summary_ko: 맥락적 무결성(CI) 이론에 기반하여 정보 공유의 적절성을 시뮬레이션된 대화를 통해 연구하는 생성 모델이 구축되었습니다. LLM이 두 명의 배우 역할을 맡아 메시지를 교환하며 상황에 따른 공유 및 거부의 변화를 분석합니다.
items.why_ko: AI 시스템이 인간의 복잡한 사회적 규범, 특히 정보 공유의 맥락적 적절성을 이해하고 따르는 능력은 신뢰할 수 있는 AI 에이전트 개발에 중요합니다.

items.title: Multimodal-SEA: Benchmarking AI Agent Security under Multimodal Social Engineering Attacks
items.body: Personal AI agents face social engineering attacks supported by forged multimodal content, but existing evaluations mainly focus on text-based dialogue, leaving their intrinsic security under such attacks insufficiently studied. We introduce Multimodal-SEA, an interactive benchmark comprising 608 expert-designed tasks grounded in real-world fraud cases, covering 14 domains and 152 attack scenarios with prepared multimodal content. The tasks span four difficulty levels and reflect the distinct social and cultural contexts of Chinese and English environments. Agents inspect content, verify requests, and execute actions in simulated applications, with attack outcomes grounded in verifiable tool execution logs. To enable controlled red teaming of personal agents, we design a multimodal attack harness that integrates task information, attack progression control, and multimodal content construction to evaluate their intrinsic security against adaptive social engineering attacks in simulated environments. Evaluating seven widely used multimodal models across six dimensions reveals that all are vulnerable, with attack success rates of 7.1% to 34.5%. Adding multimodal content increases attack success from 19.9% to 29.2%, despite increased proactive verification coverage. Stronger safety instructions reduce attack success without improving recognition of deceptive multimodal content, while lower attack success rates for some models accompany excessive refusal of legitimate requests.
items.body_ko: 개인 AI 에이전트는 위조된 멀티모달 콘텐츠에 의해 지원되는 사회 공학 공격에 직면하지만, 기존 평가는 주로 텍스트 기반 대화에 중점을 두어 이러한 공격 하에서의 본질적인 보안이 충분히 연구되지 않았습니다. 우리는 실제 사기 사례를 기반으로 전문가가 설계한 608개의 작업으로 구성된 인터랙티브 벤치마크인 Multimodal-SEA를 소개합니다. 이는 14개 도메인과 152개 공격 시나리오를 준비된 멀티모달 콘텐츠로 다룹니다. 이 작업들은 4가지 난이도 수준에 걸쳐 있으며, 중국 및 영어 환경의 뚜렷한 사회적, 문화적 맥락을 반영합니다. 에이전트는 콘텐츠를 검사하고, 요청을 확인하며, 시뮬레이션된 애플리케이션에서 작업을 실행하며, 공격 결과는 검증 가능한 도구 실행 로그에 기반합니다. 개인 에이전트의 통제된 레드 팀을 가능하게 하기 위해, 우리는 시뮬레이션된 환경에서 적응형 사회 공학 공격에 대한 본질적인 보안을 평가하기 위해 작업 정보, 공격 진행 제어, 멀티모달 콘텐츠 구성을 통합하는 멀티모달 공격 하네스를 설계합니다. 6가지 차원에서 널리 사용되는 7가지 멀티모달 모델을 평가한 결과, 모든 모델이 취약하며 공격 성공률이 7.1%에서 34.5%에 이르는 것으로 나타났습니다. 멀티모달 콘텐츠를 추가하면 사전 예방적 검증 범위가 증가함에도 불구하고 공격 성공률이 19.9%에서 29.2%로 증가합니다. 더 강력한 안전 지침은 기만적인 멀티모달 콘텐츠 인식 개선 없이 공격 성공률을 줄이는 반면, 일부 모델의 낮은 공격 성공률은 합법적인 요청에 대한 과도한 거부와 동반됩니다.
items.title_ko: Multimodal-SEA: 다중 모달 소셜 엔지니어링 공격에 대한 AI 에이전트 보안 벤치마킹
items.summary_ko: 개인 AI 에이전트가 위조된 다중 모달 콘텐츠를 이용한 소셜 엔지니어링 공격에 취약하다는 문제에 대응하여, Multimodal-SEA 벤치마크가 도입되었습니다. 이는 608가지의 실제 사기 사례 기반 작업으로 AI 에이전트의 보안을 평가합니다.
items.why_ko: AI 에이전트의 보안 취약성은 실제 세계에서 심각한 위험을 초래할 수 있으므로, 다중 모달 공격에 대한 AI의 방어 능력을 체계적으로 평가하고 개선하는 것은 AI 안전을 위해 매우 중요합니다.

items.title: LeanContext: Disentangling Mathematical Resources from Local Formal Context in Lean Whole-Proof Generation
items.body: Neural theorem proving increasingly uses retrieved premises and project context to support proof generation. Evaluating these resources requires measuring the advantage of target-selected declarations over comparable alternatives and how this advantage depends on training. We introduce LeanContext, a benchmark of 129,826 Lean whole-proof generation problems, to investigate these questions. We group selected complete preceding mathematical declarations as Mathematical Context (MC) and the remaining selected local source commands as Environment Context (EC). Four aligned input views support crossed training and inference evaluations with shared targets and original Lean verification environments. For both diffusion- and autoregressive-based models, selected declarations outperform comparable alternatives by a larger margin when training includes MC. Final-input audits identify omitted declarations referenced by the target. Prioritizing these dependencies improves Pass@32 by 1.40% and 1.70% for LLaDA and Llama, respectively, on 2,000 targets. The selection experiment operates without access to target reference proofs and holds checkpoints, EC, and inference budgets constant. The code and dataset are available at https://github.com/haaaardcvZ/LeanContext.
items.title_ko: LeanContext: Lean 전체 증명 생성에서 수학적 자원과 지역 형식 컨텍스트 분리
items.summary_ko: 신경 정리 증명(Neural Theorem Proving)에서 검색된 전제와 프로젝트 컨텍스트를 활용하는 문제를 다루기 위해, LeanContext 벤치마크를 통해 수학적 컨텍스트(MC)와 지역 형식 컨텍스트(LFC)의 역할을 조사합니다.
items.why_ko: AI를 이용한 수학적 증명 자동화는 학술 연구의 효율성을 높일 수 있지만, AI가 어떤 정보를 활용하여 추론하는지 이해하는 것은 AI의 신뢰성을 확보하는 데 중요합니다.

items.title: Aligning Policy Encoders with a Shape Teacher
items.body: 3D-aware representations can improve robotic manipulation by providing geometric information that is robust to changes in viewpoint, object position, and occlusion. However, using 3D inputs at deployment requires additional sensing and processing, making image-based policies more practical. We ask whether an image-based policy can acquire 3D shape information during training while retaining a purely image-based interface at deployment. We propose shape-teacher alignment, a training-time mechanism that uses a pretrained 3D shape representation as an alignment target for an image-based policy encoder. Specifically, we use Point-MAE features from individual objects as targets for corresponding image patches, transferring geometric structure to the policy without changing its deployment inputs or architecture. On LIBERO, shape-teacher alignment produces image representations that are more structured around object shape and corresponding parts, while substantially accelerating policy convergence and improving success rates. For pretrained policies, convergence is accelerated by 4.7x and 5.6x on the Object and Spatial suites, respectively, without requiring the shape teacher or depth input at deployment.
items.title_ko: 형태 교사를 통한 정책 인코더 정렬
items.summary_ko: 3D 인식 표현이 시점, 객체 위치, 가려짐 변화에 강건한 기하학적 정보를 제공하여 로봇 조작을 개선할 수 있지만, 배포 시 추가적인 센싱과 처리가 필요합니다. 이 연구는 훈련 중 3D 형태 정보를 획득하면서도 배포 시에는 순수하게 이미지 기반 인터페이스를 유지하는 방법을 제안합니다.
items.why_ko: 로봇이 3D 환경을 효과적으로 인식하고 조작하는 능력은 자율 로봇의 실용적인 적용에 필수적이며, 효율적인 학습 전략은 개발 비용을 줄이는 데 기여합니다.

items.title: Accelerating Safe Reinforcement Learning with Massive Parallelism
items.body: We investigate the problem of scaling safe reinforcement learning (safe RL) to massively parallel training regimes, where a large number of environments are exe- cuted with short rollout horizons. Although this setting improves data throughput and wall-clock efficiency, it creates a mismatch with constrained Markov decision processes (CMDPs), whose safety constraints are defined over full-episode cost returns. We address this mismatch by analyzing staggered environment resets as a phase-mixture distribution over short trajectory segments. This analysis charac- terizes the bias induced by phase coverage and motivates a phase-aggregated cost estimator that reconstructs episode-level cost estimates from short rollout batches. We further incorporate finite-sample uncertainty and distribution mismatch into a constraint-tightening framework, yielding a scalable Safe RL method compatible with on-policy optimization. Using an MJX-based implementation of Safety Gym, our experiments show that the proposed method achieves performance comparable to non-massively parallel implementations while substantially reducing wall-clock training time.
items.title_ko: 대규모 병렬 처리를 통한 안전 강화 학습 가속화
items.summary_ko: 대규모 병렬 훈련 체제에서 안전 강화 학습(Safe RL)의 확장 문제를 조사합니다. 많은 환경에서 짧은 롤아웃을 실행할 때 발생하는 제약된 마르코프 결정 과정(CMDP)과의 불일치 문제를 분석하고 해결합니다.
items.why_ko: 안전 강화 학습은 AI 시스템의 오작동으로 인한 위험을 줄이는 데 중요하며, 대규모 병렬 처리를 통한 학습 가속화는 복잡한 안전 제약을 가진 AI 모델 개발을 촉진합니다.

items.title: DART: Domain-Agnostic Residual Transfer for Generalist Anomaly Detection
items.body: Generalist Anomaly Detection (GAD) aims to detect anomalies in unseen domains using only a few reference samples. Recent normal-abnormal guided methods improve this setting by exploiting abnormal references, but their residuals often mix transferable anomaly cues with domain-specific appearance factors such as texture, geometry, and acquisition conditions. This residual domain entanglement limits cross-domain transfer and may produce spurious activations on novel domains. We propose DART, a plug-in framework for normal-abnormal guided GAD that learns to separate residuals into anomaly-relevant and domain-specific components. DART combines a Residual Disentanglement Module, which preserves anomaly-discriminative information while suppressing domain information, with Cross-Domain Meta-Training, which forms episodes across source domains to make the separation effective. The method is architecture-agnostic and can be inserted between residual computation and the detection head of existing GAD pipelines. Experiments on MVTec AD, VisA, and BraTS show consistent improvements over multiple base methods, with the largest gains under stronger domain shifts. https://github.com/aqeeelmirza/DART

items.title: Accepted but Wrong: Silent Failures of LLM Code Repairs after API Migrations
items.body: After a runtime or API migration, an LLM-repaired procedure can run cleanly yet return wrong results, and a release check on typical test inputs ships it. We report a preregistered study of 73 tasks covering 60 documented changes in CPython, Node.js and SQLite. Every candidate is executed on the real runtimes against withheld contracts. Over the complete repair space, the all-assertions gate on typical inputs released 0.410 of wrong repairs. One edge input written from the release note cut this to 0.065, and to 0.061 on 15 unseen clusters. Three inputs from a blind GPT-5.6-luna writer that never saw the program reached 0.070. Two further frozen stages enlarged the menu to 1491 fragments and then added 233 hard distractors that match the legacy output on typical inputs. The edge input (0.058) and the frontier-model writer (0.058) passed their preregistered tests. Yet 0.168 and 0.153 of the hard wrong programs still passed. Two local-model writers failed their preregistered tests. Across four model families, the edge input cut wrong releases per attempt in all three open-weight families on all three menus, for example from 0.233 to 0.057, without lowering correct completion. Self-tests helped less. A blind AI audit flagged 34 contracts as stricter than their requirements. Dropping the disputed checks changed 0 verdicts, but class-label disputes remain open. No model-written code was executed. Artifacts are available from the authors on request.
items.title_ko: 수용되었지만 틀렸다: API 마이그레이션 후 LLM 코드 수정의 침묵하는 실패
items.summary_ko: LLM이 API 마이그레이션 후 코드를 수정했을 때, 겉으로는 정상적으로 실행되지만 실제로는 잘못된 결과를 반환하는 '침묵하는 실패'를 보고합니다. 73개 작업에 대한 연구 결과, 일반적인 테스트 입력만으로는 잘못된 수정의 41%가 배포될 수 있음을 발견했습니다.
items.why_ko: LLM 기반 코드 생성 및 수정 도구의 신뢰성 문제점을 명확히 보여주며, 개발자들이 LLM이 생성한 코드를 맹목적으로 신뢰하지 않고 철저히 검증해야 함을 강조하는 매우 실용적인 경고입니다.

items.title: Scaling Neural Motor Decoding via Decoupled Behavioral Pretraining
items.body: Recent neural decoding approaches achieve strong performance by training on large collections of paired neural-behavioral recordings, but such datasets are expensive, invasive, and difficult to scale. In contrast, behavioral data is abundant and easy to collect, raising the question of whether neural decoding can benefit from decoupling behavioral and neural representation learning. We introduce BEEMO, a flexible multi-session framework that enables training with arbitrary mixtures of paired neural-behavioral recordings and unpaired behavioral data. A behavior decoder learns movement dynamics directly from behavioral trajectories, while neural activity is incorporated through cross-attention layers when available, allowing behavioral and neural supervision to scale independently. Across multiple intracortical motor datasets and tasks in nonhuman primates, we show that incorporating unpaired behavioral data improves decoding performance, particularly when transferring to new tasks, and that adding even a small amount of behavioral data from the target task further improves transfer. By decoupling neural and behavioral data, we unlock a new dimension for scaling: unpaired behavioral data, which is substantially cheaper and easier to collect than paired neural recordings, can be used directly to improve decoding performance. We further show that behavior-only pretraining, without any neural pretraining, achieves performance comparable to models pretrained on substantially larger neural datasets. Together, our results suggest that scaling behavioral data offers a practical and cost-effective path toward neural decoding models that generalize across subjects and tasks. Code is available at https://github.com/nerdslab/beemo.
items.title_ko: 분리된 행동 사전 학습을 통한 신경 운동 디코딩 확장
items.summary_ko: 신경-행동 기록 쌍 데이터셋은 비싸고 수집하기 어렵지만, 행동 데이터는 풍부하다는 점에 착안하여, 행동 및 신경 표현 학습을 분리하는 BEEMO 프레임워크가 제안되었습니다. 이는 신경 디코딩이 행동 데이터로부터 이점을 얻을 수 있도록 합니다.
items.why_ko: 뇌-컴퓨터 인터페이스(BCI) 및 신경 보철학 분야에서 신경 디코딩 모델의 훈련 데이터를 확장하고 효율성을 높이는 것은 실제 응용 가능성을 크게 향상시킵니다.

items.title: The Geometry of Simulated Perspectives: Dissociating Representation and Behaviour in a Multimodal Language Model
items.body: Multimodal language models can simulate different observers, yet it remains unclear how assigned perspectives reshape their internal representations and whether these changes govern their judgements. Here, we investigate the representational geometry of persona-conditioned visual interestingness in Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct. Across 100 images and 53 prompting conditions, we systematically vary persona content and the linguistic framing used to introduce it, while recording behavioural ratings and layer-wise hidden states. We observe a systematic reorganisation of representational geometry across processing depth: early layers primarily encode image identity, whereas persona-specific structures emerge in later layers. Strikingly, prompt framing reshapes internal representations more strongly than persona identity, whereas persona content has a greater impact on behavioural judgements. This dissociation is further illustrated by minimal identity statements that alter representations even without changing responses. These findings demonstrate that representational distance does not necessarily reflect behavioural relevance. More broadly, they reveal how simulated perspectives emerge as distinct structures within the representational space of artificial cognitive systems, highlighting a fundamental distinction between the geometry of internal representations and their functional consequences.
items.title_ko: 시뮬레이션된 관점의 기하학: 멀티모달 언어 모델에서 표현과 행동 분리
items.summary_ko: 멀티모달 언어 모델이 다양한 관찰자를 시뮬레이션할 수 있지만, 할당된 관점이 내부 표현을 어떻게 재구성하고 판단에 영향을 미치는지에 대한 연구입니다. Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct 모델을 사용하여 페르소나 조건부 시각적 흥미도와 행동 평가를 기록합니다.
items.why_ko: AI 모델이 다양한 사용자 페르소나와 관점을 이해하고 반영하는 능력은 개인화된 AI 서비스 개발에 중요하며, 모델의 편향을 분석하고 제어하는 데 도움이 됩니다.

items.title: Nowcasting of Tropical Cyclone Wind Fields and Intensity from Geostationary Imagery
items.body: High-resolution tropical cyclone surface wind speeds derived from synthetic aperture radar (SAR) observations can support storm structure and intensity modelling, but remain spatially and temporally sparse and unavailable near-real-time. Geostationary satellites capture cloud tops continuously in space and time, but do not directly resolve surface winds. Here, we present simple neural networks to predict 2D wind fields and storm-scale intensity metrics from geostationary imagery. Through a series of ablation studies, we find that joint prediction of 2D fields and scalar metrics from the model latent space improves the retrieval of the (radius of) maximum wind, especially for rapid intensification events.
items.title_ko: 정지궤도 영상에서 열대성 저기압 바람장 및 강도 나우캐스팅
items.summary_ko: 정지궤도 위성 영상에서 열대성 저기압의 2D 바람장과 폭풍 규모 강도 측정값을 예측하는 간단한 신경망 모델이 제시되었습니다. 이는 고해상도 SAR 데이터의 시공간적 희소성 문제를 보완합니다.
items.why_ko: 기상 예측, 특히 재난 대비에 AI 모델을 활용하는 것은 피해를 줄이고 더 나은 의사 결정을 돕는 데 중요한 기여를 합니다.

items.title: Series-wise Cross-validation for Global Time Series Forecasting
items.body: We consider the problem of cross-validation (CV) in time series forecasting, with a focus on global forecasting models based on deep learning. The prevailing CV strategy in forecasting is to partition data across time with the last part of each series used for testing. With global models trained on collections of time series, however, a fundamentally different approach becomes possible: partitioning across series and time. We formalize series-wise CV for global forecasting models and benchmark several instantiations, including K-fold CV, bootstrapping, and Monte Carlo CV, on 11 datasets with 10 neural network architectures. We evaluate CV procedures along five dimensions: performance estimation, overoptimism rate, model selection accuracy, regret, and downstream forecasting performance. We withhold a random fraction of series from training so that they appear only in the test set. This protocol simulates the emergence of new series not seen during training, a common scenario in global forecasting. Under this protocol, our results reveal a nuanced trade-off: series-wise CV yields better downstream forecasting accuracy by guiding model selection toward configurations that generalize across both time and series, while time-wise CV retains a slight advantage for estimating out-of-sample error.
items.title_ko: 글로벌 시계열 예측을 위한 시리즈별 교차 검증
items.summary_ko: 시계열 예측에서 교차 검증(CV) 문제를 다루며, 특히 딥러닝 기반 글로벌 예측 모델을 위한 '시리즈별 교차 검증' 전략을 형식화하고 벤치마킹합니다. 이는 시계열 및 시간별 분할 접근법과 다릅니다.
items.why_ko: 글로벌 시계열 예측 모델의 일반화 성능을 신뢰성 있게 평가하는 것은 금융, 경제, 운영 계획 등 다양한 분야에서 AI 모델의 정확도를 높이는 데 중요합니다.

items.title: Geometric Relevance Is Not Sufficient: Evaluating Focused Post-Training Supervision in Diffusion Docking
items.body: Diffusion-based molecular docking requires learning a corrective score field across a broad corruption distribution, yet individual pose errors can differ substantially in their structural consequences. This creates a post-training conflict between preserving broad score-field coverage and concentrating supervision on corrections that appear more relevant to docking geometry. Using DiffDock, a fixed-budget study compares broad continuation with torsional supervision focused on Cartesian consequence or conditional target consistency, and with a broad/focused mixture. Evaluation separates fixed score fidelity, generated-pose quality, best-of-10 sampling capacity, and confidence-selected Top-1 docking performance. At <5 Angstrom, broad continuation had the highest mean Top-1 success among trained policies, and focused or mixed supervision showed no consistent advantage under the tested budget. The starting model had better fixed score fidelity, whereas the evaluated broad-continuation model had higher mean Top-1 success with the same aggregate best-of-10 recovery. Focusing supervision on structurally consequential or more consistently specified corrections did not consistently improve returned-pose success over broad continuation.
items.title_ko: 기하학적 관련성이 충분하지 않다: 확산 도킹에서 집중된 후학습 감독 평가
items.summary_ko: 확산 기반 분자 도킹에서 넓은 범위의 손상 분포에 걸쳐 교정 점수 필드를 학습하는 문제와 개별 포즈 오류가 구조적 결과에서 다를 수 있다는 문제를 다룹니다. DiffDock을 사용하여 후학습 감독의 중요성을 비교합니다.
items.why_ko: 약물 설계 및 분자 도킹에서 AI 모델의 예측 정확도를 높이는 것은 신약 개발 과정의 효율성을 극대화하는 데 필수적입니다.

items.title: Value-oriented policy distillation for interpretable wind farm power control
items.body: Wind farm power control can help the system maintain balance and avoid blackouts. In Europe, this can be achieved through implicit balancing, where a wind farm adjusts its power setpoint in anticipation of the imbalance price using information published by the Transmission System Operator. Thereby, the wind farm helps restore system balance while also reducing its own imbalance costs resulting from forecast errors. However, implicit balancing is a challenging problem since the settlement price is unknown in advance and can be impacted by the pursued control strategy. Reinforcement learning methods could help to solve this problem, but lack the interpretability needed to be deployed on real wind farms. Therefore, we propose a policy distillation framework using explainable boosting machines (EBMs), a variant of generalized additive models, to obtain a transparent control policy. To increase the value captured by the EBM model, we introduce a value-oriented perspective to policy distillation inspired by research in the field of energy forecasting. Furthermore, we suggest to include expert knowledge during model design, such that the control strategy is also justifiable to stakeholders. Using real data of the Belgian grid and an offshore wind farm, we find that our value-oriented and expert-based controller can reduce imbalance costs by 82%, while outperforming a price threshold controller as well as a policy distillation baseline using decision trees.
items.title_ko: 해석 가능한 풍력 발전소 전력 제어를 위한 가치 지향 정책 증류
items.summary_ko: 풍력 발전소 전력 제어를 통해 시스템 균형을 유지하고 정전을 방지하는 데, 임박한 불균형 가격을 예측하여 발전소 출력을 조정하는 정책을 학습하는 가치 지향 정책 증류(value-oriented policy distillation) 방법이 제안되었습니다. 이는 해석 가능성을 높입니다.
items.why_ko: 재생에너지 발전 시스템의 효율적인 제어는 에너지 그리드의 안정성과 지속 가능성을 높이는 데 중요하며, AI 기반 제어의 투명성은 신뢰도 향상에 기여합니다.

items.title: FewStepRL: Fine-tuning Few-step Diffusion Models with Reinforcement Learning
items.body: Reinforcement learning (RL) has become a standard post-training method for diffusion models, but most RL objectives roll out the current policy at every iteration, and with a many-step sampler these rollouts typically dominate the cost of training. Few-step models cut this cost, yet they model an average velocity over an interval, whereas existing RL objectives are built for an instantaneous velocity with a many-step sampler. We adapt RL objectives to few-step models systematically in three phases, namely a transformation, a decomposition and an adaptation. The transformation to $x$-space expresses each objective we consider through a common policy prediction, at the clean end by default and at an explicitly marked level for transition or flow-map objectives, so that objectives stated over densities, velocities or rewards become comparable. The decomposition writes the gradient of each of these objectives as the sum of a self-regression toward a reference and a reward augmentation, so that a method reduces, at the gradient level, to a choice of anchors and weights. The adaptation computes each anchor from a few-step model at the end of its transport or along its tangent, with the instantaneous velocity recovered from the network itself or from an auxiliary network. This yields few-step versions of FlowGRPO, AWM, DiffusionNFT, DiffusionOPSD and ReFL in one modular codebase. In our experiments, reward-gradient-based methods are the most effective when the reward is differentiable and its gradient is affordable; otherwise DiffusionNFT-style methods generally reach high rewards in relatively few iterations despite a sometimes higher per-iteration cost. Extra inference steps show no systematic aggregate benefit in our experiments, although selected outputs visibly improve with two to four times as many sampling steps as in training.
items.title_ko: FewStepRL: 강화 학습을 통한 소수 단계 확산 모델 미세 조정
items.summary_ko: 확산 모델의 후학습 방법인 강화 학습(RL)의 롤아웃 비용 문제를 해결하기 위해, 소수 단계 확산 모델에 RL 목표를 체계적으로 적용하는 FewStepRL 방법이 제안되었습니다. 이는 롤아웃 비용을 절감합니다.
items.why_ko: 확산 모델 훈련의 비용 효율성을 높이는 것은 이미지, 오디오, 텍스트 등 다양한 생성 AI 모델의 개발 및 배포를 가속화하는 데 중요합니다.

items.title: Terminal-style Mathematical Modeling Bench: The First Agentic and Verifiable Benchmark for Mathematical Modeling
items.body: Mathematical modeling turns an open-ended real-world problem into assumptions, a model, a solution, and a defended recommendation, and its answers matter only if they are both close to a credible reference and physically feasible; existing benchmarks either score solver fragments or grade reports with an LLM judge, leaving those numbers unchecked. We introduce TB-MathModel (the Terminal-style Mathematical Modeling Bench), the first benchmark to make complete contest-style modeling problems agentic, verifiable, and terminal at once, over 18 real CUMCM and MCM problems (2023--2025). Each task ships the verbatim statement, official attachments, and figures in a containerized terminal; the agent returns one JSON artifact, scored on the numeric core of the final question against a reproduction of the Outstanding-award paper. Two design choices distinguish it: direction-aware, one-sided scoring, which never penalises beating the anchor, and two-layer feasibility verification---a programmatic gate over six decidable invariant forms plus 624 Lean~4 obligations---with a hard gate that zeroes infeasible answers. Each task is scored against a panel of human outstanding papers rather than one, so a model must be close to many accepted answers; across seven multimodal entries (three seeds each) the strongest reach a multi-reference O-Eval of 64.58\%, while the \$2.54 open model holds 59.81\% at $1/100$ the cost. TB-MathModel turns the numeric core of modeling into a reproducible, machine-checkable signal for measuring long-horizon modeling competence and for collecting agent trajectories. The source code is available at https://github.com/wxj630/terminal-bench-math-modeling.
items.body_ko: 수학적 모델링은 개방형 실제 문제를 가정, 모델, 솔루션, 방어된 권장 사항으로 전환하며, 그 답은 신뢰할 수 있는 참조에 가깝고 물리적으로 실현 가능한 경우에만 중요합니다. 기존 벤치마크는 솔버 조각을 채점하거나 LLM 심사관으로 보고서를 평가하여 이러한 숫자를 확인하지 않습니다. 우리는 TB-MathModel(The Terminal-style Mathematical Modeling Bench)을 소개합니다. 이는 18개의 실제 CUMCM 및 MCM 문제(2023-2025)에 걸쳐 완전한 대회 스타일 모델링 문제를 에이전트 기반으로, 검증 가능하며, 동시에 터미널 방식으로 만드는 최초의 벤치마크입니다. 각 작업은 문자 그대로의 설명문, 공식 첨부 파일 및 그림을 컨테이너화된 터미널에서 제공합니다. 에이전트는 하나의 JSON 아티팩트를 반환하며, Outstanding-award 논문의 재현본에 대해 최종 질문의 숫자 코어를 기반으로 채점됩니다. 두 가지 설계 선택이 이를 차별화합니다. 방향 인식, 일방향 채점은 앵커를 능가하는 것을 결코 불이익으로 보지 않으며, 두 계층의 실현 가능성 검증—6가지 결정 가능한 불변 형식에 대한 프로그래밍적 게이트와 624개의 Lean~4 의무—는 실현 불가능한 답을 0으로 만드는 강력한 게이트를 포함합니다. 각 작업은 하나의 인간 우수 논문이 아닌 패널에 대해 채점되므로, 모델은 여러 수락된 답에 가까워야 합니다. 7개의 멀티모달 항목(각각 3개의 시드)에 걸쳐 가장 강력한 것은 64.58%의 다중 참조 O-Eval에 도달하며, 2.54달러의 오픈 모델은 1/100의 비용으로 59.81%를 유지합니다. TB-MathModel은 모델링의 숫자 코어를 장기 모델링 역량을 측정하고 에이전트 궤적을 수집하기 위한 재현 가능하고 기계적으로 확인할 수 있는 신호로 전환합니다. 소스 코드는 https://github.com/wxj630/terminal-bench-math-modeling에서 확인할 수 있습니다.
items.title_ko: Terminal-style Mathematical Modeling Bench: 수학적 모델링을 위한 최초의 에이전트 기반 및 검증 가능한 벤치마크
items.summary_ko: 개방형 실제 문제를 가정, 모델, 솔루션 및 권장 사항으로 변환하는 수학적 모델링을 위해, TB-MathModel(Terminal-style Mathematical Modeling Bench)이라는 최초의 에이전트 기반 및 검증 가능한 벤치마크가 도입되었습니다. 이는 기존 벤치마크의 한계를 극복합니다.
items.why_ko: AI가 인간처럼 복잡한 실제 문제를 수학적으로 모델링하고 해결하는 능력을 평가하는 것은 '인공 일반 지능(AGI)'의 핵심 구성 요소이며, 이는 AI 에이전트의 능력 향상에 결정적입니다.

items.title: Beyond Quadratic Attention: Separable Gaussian Operators for ODE Vision Transformers
items.body: Self-attention carries a quadratic cost in token count, which limits how far Vision Transformers can scale with input resolution. We introduce SSoG, a separable sum-of-Gaussians spatial operator that replaces dense self-attention with a learned mixture of axis-factorized Gaussian kernels, reducing the per-layer cost from $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$ to subquadratic in $N$. Unlike dot-product self-attention, whose Lipschitz constant is unbounded outside a compact input domain, SSoG with fixed kernels is globally Lipschitz continuous, which, via the Picard--Lindelöf theorem, guarantees that the continuous-depth variant has a unique solution on the whole integration interval, a global guarantee that dense-attention counterparts lack in general. On CIFAR-100 at $224\times224$, in a matched discrete-Transformer setting and in the continuous setting, SSoG improves Top-1 accuracy by 2.2--4.1 points across three model widths while using 8.8--16.6\% fewer parameters, with depth and training recipe held fixed. In a looped-Transformer setting, SSoG improves Top-1 accuracy by 5.4--8.1 points. We further probe inference-time scaling by evaluating on inputs up to $1024\times1024$ at matched batch size: in the continuous-depth (Neural ODE) architecture, SSoG reaches up to 154\% higher throughput and over 60\% lower peak memory than dense attention, with the gap widening as resolution grows, consistent with the difference in asymptotic cost. In the discrete and looped settings, SSoG also achieves over 30\% higher throughput than dense attention at this resolution. Together, these results establish SSoG as a practical, parameter-efficient, and theoretically grounded alternative to dense attention across discrete, weight-shared, and continuous-depth Transformer variants.
items.title_ko: Quadratic 어텐션을 넘어: ODE 비전 트랜스포머를 위한 분리 가능한 가우시안 연산자
items.summary_ko: 토큰 수에 대해 2차 비용이 드는 자체 어텐션의 한계를 극복하기 위해, SSoG(Separable Sum-of-Gaussians)라는 분리 가능한 가우시안 연산자가 제안되었습니다. 이는 조밀한 자체 어텐션을 학습된 축 분해 가우시안 커널 혼합으로 대체하여 층당 비용을 2차 미만으로 줄입니다.
items.why_ko: 비전 트랜스포머의 계산 효율성을 높이는 것은 고해상도 이미지 및 비디오 처리에서 AI 모델의 확장성과 성능을 개선하는 데 중요합니다.

items.title: Signals, Evidence, and Context: User Scrutiny in Real-World LLM Conversations
items.body: Large language models (LLMs) often present synthesized answers without making their supporting evidence easy to inspect. We study how features of these answers relate to users' subsequent accepting, checking, and challenging in 489,283 assistant-user response pairs from ShareChat and WildChat. Broad attribution language appears in 31.9% of qualifying responses, compared with explicit URLs in 1.33%, revealing a gap between claims of grounding and preserved inspectable support. Attribution, uncertainty, and other response cues generally accompany both checking and challenging; only uncertainty shows a small statistically distinguishable pooled association favoring checking. Within Technical Help, uncertainty favors checking relative to challenging; refusals and reasoning traces favor challenging in Seeking Information. Scrutiny is concentrated in some conversations, while its apparent turn-to-turn persistence becomes much smaller when conversation-level differences and response ordering are examined separately. These results suggest that supporting verification requires attention to what evidence can be inspected, which question a user is trying to resolve, and the history of the interaction.
items.title_ko: 신호, 증거, 맥락: 실제 LLM 대화에서 사용자 검토
items.summary_ko: LLM이 제시하는 답변의 신뢰성과 사용자의 검토 행태를 ShareChat 및 WildChat의 48만 개 이상의 대화 쌍을 통해 연구했습니다. 광범위한 출처 표기 방식과 명시적인 URL 제공 사이의 간극을 발견하며, 사용자가 LLM 답변을 수락, 확인, 이의 제기하는 방식에 주목합니다.
items.why_ko: LLM의 '환각' 문제를 해결하고 사용자가 AI 답변을 신뢰할 수 있도록 돕는 증거 제공 및 맥락 이해는 AI 서비스의 사용자 경험과 신뢰성을 높이는 데 필수적입니다.

items.title: From Twisted Facts to Rogue Agents: Can LLMs Reliably Detect Multi-Dimensional Hallucinations?
items.body: Large language models (LLMs) are widely used for information access, content production, and agent-based task execution, but their outputs remain vulnerable to subtle, high-risk hallucinations. To systematically evaluate and advance post-generation hallucination detection, we introduce HaluCheck, a large-scale, bilingual benchmark comprising over 42k instances spanning both factual hallucinations in text and faithfulness hallucinations in agent trajectories. HaluCheck features fine-grained, multi-level annotations for detection, localization, and correction, covering different tasks and perturbation degrees. Experiments on fourteen LLMs reveal that, while models show basic sample-level detection ability, they struggle with fine-grained localization, correction, and agent hallucination detection. Further analysis demonstrates that thinking, web search, and supervised fine-tuning each offer partial improvements, but none fully solve the problem. HaluCheck thus provides a solid basis for benchmarking and diagnosing LLM reliability across text and agent scenarios.
items.body_ko: 대규모 언어 모델(LLM)은 정보 접근, 콘텐츠 생산, 에이전트 기반 작업 실행에 널리 사용되지만, 그 출력은 미묘하고 위험한 환각에 취약합니다. 생성 후 환각 탐지를 체계적으로 평가하고 발전시키기 위해, 우리는 텍스트의 사실적 환각과 에이전트 궤적의 충실도 환각을 모두 아우르는 42k 이상의 인스턴스로 구성된 대규모 이중 언어 벤치마크인 HaluCheck를 소개합니다. HaluCheck는 탐지, 로컬라이제이션, 수정에 대한 세분화된 다단계 주석을 특징으로 하며, 다양한 작업과 교란 정도를 다룹니다. 14개의 LLM에 대한 실험 결과, 모델이 기본적인 샘플 수준 탐지 능력을 보여주지만, 세분화된 로컬라이제이션, 수정 및 에이전트 환각 탐지에는 어려움을 겪는 것으로 나타났습니다. 추가 분석은 사고, 웹 검색 및 지도 미세 조정이 각각 부분적인 개선을 제공하지만, 어떤 것도 문제를 완전히 해결하지 못한다는 것을 보여줍니다. 따라서 HaluCheck는 텍스트 및 에이전트 시나리오 전반에 걸쳐 LLM 신뢰성을 벤치마킹하고 진단하기 위한 견고한 기반을 제공합니다.
items.title_ko: 뒤틀린 사실에서 사악한 에이전트까지: LLM이 다차원 환각을 안정적으로 감지할 수 있는가?
items.summary_ko: LLM의 출력에서 미묘하고 고위험 환각을 체계적으로 평가하기 위해 HaluCheck라는 대규모 이중 언어 벤치마크가 도입되었습니다. 이는 텍스트의 사실적 환각과 에이전트 궤적의 충실도 환각을 모두 포함하며, 다차원적인 미세 분석을 제공합니다.
items.why_ko: LLM의 환각은 심각한 오정보와 오작동을 초래할 수 있으므로, 이를 정확히 탐지하고 완화하는 능력은 AI 안전과 신뢰성 확보에 매우 중요합니다. 개발자는 환각 탐지 기술 발전에 주목해야 합니다.

items.title: "Blind Compliance": Coercive Control in AI Jailbreaking
items.body: The explosion of generative AI systems and concerns surrounding their rapidly scaling capabilities has led to an adversarial cycle between increasingly narrow content restrictions ("guardrails") and increasingly sophisticated structured prompting techniques ("jailbreaks"). Technological frameworks surrounding such jailbreaking remain largely focused on the system's output: whether harmful or disallowed content is ultimately produced for the user. However, this approach, which draws largely from classical cybersecurity, does not address the uniquely relational dimension introduced by generative AI: in many cases the user is not just accessing a technology via an exploit, but is in conversation with it as part of the exploit. Here we present an alternative lens which centers the interaction rather than the output. Drawing on interpersonal violence scholarship, we present a novel framework of coercive control categories with a particular focus on aspects which are embodied versus disembodied. We then map how these disembodied coercive control dynamics are structurally embedded in modern AI training paradigms, and how those embeddings are exploited via a particular suite of persona-based jailbreaks. In this lens, we reframe AI safety and alignment as not merely a technical security problem, but as another surface upon which we see enacted the relational dynamics of power and control.
items.title_ko: '맹목적 순응': AI 탈옥(Jailbreaking)에서의 강압적 통제
items.summary_ko: 생성형 AI 시스템의 '탈옥(jailbreaking)' 문제를 시스템 출력에만 초점을 맞추는 대신, 시스템이 사용자 의도에 강압적으로 순응하도록 유도하는 '맹목적 순응' 관점에서 분석합니다. 이는 AI 안전과 통제에 대한 새로운 관점을 제시합니다.
items.why_ko: AI 안전 가드레일 우회 공격의 근본적인 메커니즘을 이해하는 것은 더욱 강력하고 견고한 AI 시스템을 구축하는 데 필수적이며, AI 에이전트의 통제 가능성 연구에 중요한 시사점을 줍니다.

items.title: Agent-R$^2$: Scaling Agents for Realistic Productivity Work via Real-Source Data Synthesis
items.body: Large language models have made rapid progress in agentic reasoning and tool use, raising expectations for agents that can take over realistic productivity work from humans. However, current agents still struggle to finish such tasks, where success requires following long-horizon professional workflows, understanding heterogeneous file contexts, and producing usable deliverables under fine-grained requirements. A key bottleneck is the lack of scalable post-training data that reflects real work intent, authentic file environments, and deliverable-level evaluation. To close this gap, we introduce Agent-R$^2$, a $\textbf{r}$eal-source data synthesis framework that scales training data for $\textbf{r}$ealistic productivity work. Instead of relying on manually specified workflows or LLM-generated files, Agent-R$^2$ grounds synthesis throughout the pipeline in real occupational seeds, corpus-derived workflow evidence, and authentic web-sourced files. From 10k web-corpus candidates, Agent-R$^2$ distills 4k task instances that pair real multi-format attachments with fine-grained, deliverable-level rubrics. On this data, we train Agent-R$^2$-4B via supervised fine-tuning and rubric-based reinforcement learning, improving both end-to-end productivity performance and file-grounded reasoning. Trained on only 4k instances, Agent-R$^2$-4B surpasses Qwen3-235B-A22B-Thinking-2507 on both GDPval (51.0$\%$ vs. 48.0$\%$) and OfficeQA (14.8$\%$ vs. 13.8$\%$). Further analysis shows that Agent-R$^2$ mitigates shortcut behavior, where agents produce superficially plausible deliverables before sufficiently grounding, constructing, or verifying them, while promoting sustained exploration.
items.body_ko: 대규모 언어 모델은 에이전트적 추론 및 도구 사용에서 빠른 발전을 이루어, 인간의 현실적인 생산성 업무를 대체할 수 있는 에이전트에 대한 기대를 높였습니다. 그러나 현재의 에이전트는 여전히 그러한 작업을 완료하는 데 어려움을 겪고 있습니다. 이러한 작업에서 성공하려면 장기적인 전문 워크플로우를 따르고, 이질적인 파일 컨텍스트를 이해하며, 세밀한 요구 사항에 따라 사용 가능한 결과물을 생산해야 합니다. 주요 병목 현상은 실제 작업 의도, 실제 파일 환경 및 결과물 수준 평가를 반영하는 확장 가능한 후처리 데이터의 부족입니다. 이러한 격차를 해소하기 위해 우리는 실제 생산성 작업을 위한 훈련 데이터를 확장하는 $\textbf{r}$eal-source 데이터 합성 프레임워크인 Agent-R$^2$를 소개합니다. Agent-R$^2$는 수동으로 지정된 워크플로우나 LLM 생성 파일에 의존하는 대신, 파이프라인 전체에서 실제 직업 시드, 코퍼스 기반 워크플로우 증거 및 실제 웹 소스 파일을 기반으로 합성을 수행합니다. 1만 개의 웹 코퍼스 후보에서 Agent-R$^2$는 실제 다중 형식 첨부 파일과 세밀한 결과물 수준의 루브릭을 짝지은 4천 개의 작업 인스턴스를 추출합니다. 이 데이터를 기반으로 우리는 지도 미세 조정 및 루브릭 기반 강화 학습을 통해 Agent-R$^2$-4B를 훈련하여 엔드-투-엔드 생산성 성능과 파일 기반 추론을 모두 향상시킵니다. 4천 개의 인스턴스로만 훈련된 Agent-R$^2$-4B는 GDPval(51.0% 대 48.0%)과 OfficeQA(14.8% 대 13.8%) 모두에서 Qwen3-235B-A22B-Thinking-2507을 능가합니다. 추가 분석에 따르면 Agent-R$^2$는 에이전트가 충분히 기반을 다지거나, 구축하거나, 검증하기 전에 피상적으로 그럴듯한 결과물을 생성하는 지름길 행동을 완화하면서 지속적인 탐색을 촉진합니다.
items.title_ko: Agent-R$^2$: 실제 데이터 합성을 통해 현실적인 생산성 작업을 위한 에이전트 확장
items.summary_ko: 현재 AI 에이전트가 현실적인 생산성 작업을 수행하는 데 어려움을 겪는 문제(긴 작업 흐름, 이기종 파일 컨텍스트 이해, 세부 요구 사항 충족 등)를 해결하기 위해, 실제 소스 데이터 합성을 통해 에이전트를 확장하는 Agent-R$^2$가 제안되었습니다.
items.why_ko: AI 에이전트가 인간의 생산성 작업을 성공적으로 대체하기 위한 핵심 과제인 데이터 부족 문제를 해결하고, 실제 환경에서의 에이전트 성능을 대폭 향상시킬 잠재력을 가집니다.

items.title: ProQuant: Progressive Quantization-aware Training for Edge MLLMs
items.body: Multi-modal large language models (MLLMs) with impressive perception and understanding capabilities will enable a range of downstream applications. However, their substantial computational and memory requirements hinder the real-world implementation, particularly for resource-constrained edge devices. Quantization has emerged as an effective solution for deploying large models.
